keyVerseText: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
rootMeaning: The root of אֲחוֹחִי (ʼĂchôwchîy) is אַחֲוָה (ʼachăvâh), which means brotherhood or fraternity. This patronymic formation emphasizes a familial or clan relationship, specifically denoting one who belongs to a brotherly group or kinship. The literal sense of 'brother of rest' enriches the common English gloss by highlighting not only lineage but also a relational identity grounded in unity and shared heritage.
usageInScripture: The term אֲחוֹחִי appears five times in Scripture and is predominantly translated as 'the Ahohite' in four instances and 'an Ahohite' once, indicating a consistent reference to a specific clan or family group descended from Achoach. This usage underscores the word's function as a proper noun identifying members of a particular lineage within Israel, reflecting a stable ethnic and social identity across its occurrences.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲחוֹחִי as rooted in brotherhood reminds believers that God’s people are called into a familial relationship that transcends mere ancestry. This term invites reflection on the unity and mutual support that characterize the community of faith, mirroring the spiritual brotherhood found in Christ. It also highlights God's providential preservation of His people through distinct clans and families, each with a role in His redemptive plan. Recognizing this deep connection enriches our appreciation of the covenant community as a spiritual family bound by faith and grace.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 23:9, Eleazar is identified as 'the son of Dodo the Ahohite,' emphasizing his belonging to this brotherly clan. This designation not only situates Eleazar within a specific lineage but also connects him to the legacy of faithful warriors who stood with David. The word אֲחוֹחִי here conveys more than heritage; it signifies a trusted member of God’s people who courageously upheld Israel in battle, reminding us that our identity in Christ calls us to steadfastness and valor in spiritual warfare.
